question: The Harappan city of Dholavira was divided into how many parts?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Harappan city of Dholavira was divided into **three main parts**.
 
• The three parts are known as the **citadel, the middle town, and the lower town**.
 
• This division is significant as it highlights the **advanced planning and architectural skills** of the Harappan civilization.
 
• The citadel was the most important part, housing the ruling class, while the middle and lower towns were inhabited by the common people and artisans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harappan Civilization**

 
 
• The Harappan Civilization, also known as the Indus Valley Civilization, was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, flourishing around 2500 BCE in the northwestern regions of South Asia.
 
• This civilization is noted for its advanced city planning, architecture, and social organization.
 
• Major cities of the Harappan Civilization include Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, and Dholavira.
 
• The civilization was characterized by its impressive public infrastructure, including well-planned streets, drainage systems, and large public baths.
 
 
 
• **Dholavira**
 
 
• Dholavira is an archaeological site located in the Kutch district of Gujarat, India.
 
• It is one of the largest and most prominent Harappan sites discovered so far.
 
• The site was excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and has provided valuable insights into the urban planning and social structure of the Harappan civilization.
 
• Dholavira is known for its sophisticated water conservation systems and unique architectural features.
 
 
 
• **Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town**
 
 
• The citadel was the high area in the city, often fortified and housing the ruling elite and important administrative and religious buildings.
 
• The middle town was where the affluent class resided, including merchants and traders.
 
• The lower town was the residential area for the common people, including artisans and laborers, and was often more densely populated.
 
• This division of the city into different parts based on function and social hierarchy is indicative of the complex and organized nature of Harappan society.
